subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - Post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlytics.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Claire,

Thanks for the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap from my side plus proposed next steps so we can validate the p95/p99 targets you mentioned:

Call highlights (from today):
- Target SLOs you asked about: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency for customer-facing API calls (including network + infer). You emphasized strict user experience requirements for the web product.
- Typical payloads: average prompt ~150 tokens, expected response ~60 tokens.
- Concurrency / throughput: you mentioned steady-state ~200 req/min (~3.3 rps) but peak bursts up to ~200 rps during batch jobs.
- Streaming: you currently stream partial tokens in the UI; preserving streaming behavior (first-token latency and incremental chunking) is important.
- Current provider ballpark: p95 ~350ms, p99 ~800ms (your ops data to confirm).

Redwood assessment notes (initial):
- For hosted API we generally see much lower p95 on similar request shapes (depends on model & quantization): p95 in the low-100s ms for small-medium prompt sizes and p99 <500ms when configured for low latency (single-tenant/priority pools).
- Key knobs that will influence end-to-end: model variant, sequence length, batching policy, concurrency isolation, and streaming-enabled pathways.

Proposed next steps (to validate with real traffic):
1) Share a short perf test plan + sample prompts (attached) we can run against your environment/sandbox or our hosted sandbox.
2) You send a small sample of provider latency logs and a typical request profile (attachments recommended). I see Claire was going to pull logs — thank you.
3) Schedule a 1-hour perf session next week (we'll run parallel tests: your current provider vs Redwood hosted with identical inputs). We'll collect p50/p95/p99, cold-start behavior, first-token time for streaming, and resource utilization.
4) If numbers look good, we can scope a short POC (2-4 weeks) with a dedicated test pool and a canary to validate at scale.

I've attached a short "redwood_perf_test_plan.pdf" with the test checklist and "test_data_prompts.json" with representative prompts.

Can you confirm:
- Which AWS region you'd prefer us to run from (us-west-2 / us-east-1 are usually quickest for our customers)?
- Do you need us to IP-allowlist service endpoints ahead of the tests?
- Availability windows next week (we have open slots Tue/Wed morning PT).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if that's easier.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_perf_test_plan.pdf (application/pdf), test_data_prompts.json (application/json)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 18:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - Post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect, appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications and the numbers we pulled from our provider this morning:

Current provider summary (running Llama-2-13B quantized, single-tenant pool):
- Typical request shape: prompt ~150 tokens / response ~60 tokens.
- Average concurrency (business hours): 20 concurrent sessions; peak concurrency observed 120 during end-of-day batch runs.
- Measured metrics (last 30 days): p50 ~220ms, p95 ~350ms, p99 ~800ms (these are end-to-end as reported by our edge + provider).
- Streaming: yes — UI requires token streaming. First-token latency currently ~220ms, then steady stream updates.

Our ideal SLO: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms for our primary interactive flow. If that’s achievable with Redwood hosted API while preserving streaming, that would be a go for us.

We will attach the recent provider summary CSV (provider_latency_summary.csv) to this thread — it contains per-path latency histograms and request sizes. Also attaching a small set of production prompts (redacted) for your tests.

Regarding the region: please run tests from us-east-1 initially (most of our customers are east coast). IP allowlist: yes, we can provide a small allowlist; send the public IPs you will use and we'll add them.

Availability: Wed 2026-09-16 09:00-11:00 PT works for our infra/ops folks.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering | Finlytics
samir.patel@finlytics.com
(650) 555-0133

Attachments: provider_latency_summary.csv (text/csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - Post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Claire,

Thanks — that data is super helpful. I've reviewed the provider summary and the numbers line up with what you described. Next steps on our side:

1) We will prepare a short Redwood-hosted configuration for the test (single-tenant priority pool + streaming-enabled runtime, model variant we'll propose: Llama-2-13B, q4_0 if you want to trade some quality for latency; we can also run an unquantized run if you prefer).
2) We'll share the public IPs for the test harness and a short pre-test checklist (CORS/allowlist, test endpoint, and test tokens).
3) Schedule confirmed: Wed 2026-09-16 09:00 PT — we'll block 2 hours in case we iterate.

For the perf session we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end), cold-start percentiles, first-byte/first-token times for streaming, concurrency scaling behaviour, and token throughput. We'll post a short recap with numbers + perf matrix within 48 hours after the run.

One question: for your internal spike tests (peak 120 concurrency), do you want us to run a burst test that mimics that pattern, or focus first on steady-state and streaming-first-token behaviour? We can do both, but want to prioritize what matters most for your launch.

Looking forward — I'll send the IPs + checklist by EOD today.

Best,
Marissa
